payload.title: genesis_lifecycle.__all__ omits the public reader eval_window_entered_at that genesis_superiority imports by name, and genesis_lifecycle is not one of the modules whose __all__ is pinned to its public definitions
evidence: aria-kernel/aria_kernel/genesis_lifecycle.py:581-596 (__all__ lists every other public name and not eval_window_entered_at)
aria-kernel/aria_kernel/genesis_superiority.py:44 (production code imports the reader by name)
aria-kernel/tests/test_module_export_surfaces.py:19-23 (the registered modules are autonomy_ladder, calibrated_intelligence and own_pr_ci; genesis_lifecycle is not pinned)
payload.rule_violated: The ARIA-LOW-475 rule that a kernel module's __all__ names exactly its public top-level definitions (tests/test_module_export_surfaces.py).
payload.notes: The module's declared interface and its real one disagree: a reader, an API audit or `from aria_kernel.genesis_lifecycle import *` takes the module to offer current_lifecycle_state, lifecycle_chains and production_block_reason but not the F1.8a anchor reader, which production code already depends on. Nothing fails today, and nothing would catch the next public function that is added without an __all__ entry, because the module is outside the pinned list. Close condition: Add eval_window_entered_at to genesis_lifecycle.__all__ and add aria_kernel.genesis_lifecycle to _REGISTERED_MODULES in test_module_export_surfaces.py, so ModuleExportSurfaces.test_all_names_exactly_the_public_definitions passes for it and fails when a public definition is left out. Verified at origin/main a81bfa2d6.
